extracted.intended_audience: faculty and faculty governance bodies (and administrators) considering or implementing post-tenure review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for colleges and universities on whether and how to establish formal systems of post-tenure review that protect academic freedom and support faculty development. Includes minimum standards, procedural safeguards, and questions to ask before adopting review systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: developmental, not accountability/dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-tenure review ought to be aimed not at accountability, but at faculty development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review should not be undertaken for the purpose of dismissal; developmental ends should be paramount. Even benign developmental reviews can carry threats if not properly safeguarded. Avoid systems intended to facilitate dismissal or to redirect faculty priorities through sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty control and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-tenure review must be developed and carried out by faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty representatives involved in development should be selected by the faculty according to faculty-determined procedures. The faculty should also conduct the actual review process; procedures should conform to applicable collective bargaining agreements where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not re-evaluate tenure or shift burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-tenure review must not be a reevaluation of tenure, nor may it be used to shift the burden of proof from the institution to the faculty member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In no case should review be used to require the faculty member to 'show cause' why they should be retained. The institution must still bear the burden of proof in dismissal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect academic freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-tenure review must ensure the protection of academic freedom as defined in the 1940 Statement of Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures should not intrude on professional self-direction or be used as subterfuge for programmatic changes. Reviews that discourage controversy, risk-taking, or independence of mind diminish academic freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definition of post-tenure review
rubrics_metrics.description: Define post-tenure review as a system of periodic evaluation that goes beyond traditional forms of evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify how it differs from existing annual reports, grant/sabbatical reviews, teaching evaluations, peer review of scholarship, and accreditation program reviews — e.g., frequency, comprehensiveness, use of self-evaluations, performance objectives, feedback, and potential sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid managerial accountability replacing professional responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not substitute managerial accountability for professional responsibility in evaluating faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware proposals that shift standards from 'incompetence' to 'unsatisfactory performance' or that seek recurrently to make faculty satisfy administrative officers rather than professional standards. Such shifts can diminish academic freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain demanding standards and procedural safeguards for dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing demanding procedures and standards for dismissal must remain; post-tenure review should not ease them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dismissal is contemplated, rely on established procedures (e.g., 1940 and 1958 Statements, Recommended Institutional Regulations) that place the burden of proof on the institution and provide due process, including adversarial hearings and opportunities to confront witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeted reviews for identified problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a particular faculty member appears not to fulfill obligations, consider targeted review and evaluation rather than comprehensive blanket review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted review can provide developmental guidance and support to help faculty overcome difficulties without subjecting all faculty to intrusive blanket procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use reviews for programmatic or managerial objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual faculty reviews should focus on the quality of the faculty member’s work and not on larger considerations such as programmatic direction, downsizing, restructuring, or reengineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic changes should be accomplished through long-term planning and, if necessary, formal program discontinuance procedures rather than by individual reviews used to induce resignations or redirection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'fishing expeditions' for negative evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-tenure review must not become the occasion for a wide-ranging 'fishing expedition' in an attempt to dredge up negative evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should not be used to search for minor or unrelated issues to justify sanctions; they must respect the proper sphere of professional self-direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge disciplinary and career-stage differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-tenure review should be flexible enough to acknowledge different expectations in different disciplines and changing expectations at different stages of faculty careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards, expectations, and timelines may vary by field and career phase; reviews should be calibrated accordingly rather than applying uniform metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written standards developed and periodically reviewed by faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: The written standards and criteria by which faculty members are evaluated should be developed and periodically reviewed by the faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty ownership of criteria ensures legitimacy and alignment with professional norms. Periodic review of standards helps maintain relevance and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraisal standard: conscientious, professional competence
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic standard for appraisal is whether the faculty member discharges conscientiously and with professional competence the duties appropriately associated with his or her position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not evaluate against changed or more demanding tenure standards that may have arisen after the faculty member was tenured; focus on current discharge of duties rather than retroactive tenure criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of evaluation outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Except when appeals procedures require file access, the outcome of evaluations should be confidential, confined to appropriate college or university persons or bodies and the faculty member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release of results to others should occur only at the discretion or with the consent of the faculty member. Confidentiality helps prevent chilling effects on academic freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development plans must be mutual and negotiable
rubrics_metrics.description: If post-tenure review is supplemented by an individualized development plan, that plan cannot be imposed unilaterally but must be a product of mutual negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should respect academic freedom and professional self-direction, be flexible to allow alteration or abandonment, and rest on a standard of good faith from both parties rather than literal fulfillment of rigid quantitative demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty right to comment and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A faculty member should have the right to comment in response to evaluations and to challenge the findings and correct the record by appeal to an elected faculty grievance committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should also have the same rights of comment and appeal concerning how individualized development plans are formulated, their content, and any resulting evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore reassignment or separation when improvement fails
rubrics_metrics.description: If recurring evaluations reveal continuing and persistent problems not amenable to improvement, consider reassignment to other duties or separation by mutual agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no acceptable solution can be found, the administration should invoke peer consideration regarding any contemplated sanctions rather than unilaterally impose severe measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for dismissal remains 'adequate cause' and burden on institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard for dismissal or other severe sanction remains that of adequate cause; successive negative reviews do not diminish the institution's obligation to show such cause in a separate forum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation records may be admissible but are rebuttable as to accuracy. The institution must demonstrate in an adversarial proceeding that facts rise to adequate cause and afford full procedural safeguards (including cross-examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial implementation and periodic evaluation of the review system
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new system should initially be set up on a trial basis and, if continued, should itself be periodically evaluated with respect to effectiveness, cost/time, and whether it has been effectively cordoned off from disciplinary procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the system supports faculty development, redresses problems, and is sustainable without harming other academic commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do an inventory of existing procedures before creating new ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Any discussion should take into account procedures already in place (e.g., annual merit reviews, promotion reviews, programmatic and accreditation reviews) and elicit data on what existing procedures fail to address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether current processes can be augmented (e.g., a five-year review 'piggybacked' onto annual reviews) rather than creating wholly new systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key diagnostic questions before adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty bodies should ask: (a) What problems require this solution? (b) Can a system be devised based on existing procedures? (c) Is the projected review confined to developmental purposes or is it an easier route to sanctions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These questions help ensure reviews address real needs and are not covert mechanisms for weakening tenure protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide blanket vs. focused review and initiation mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether review should be 'blanket' for all tenured faculty or focused on problematic cases, and whether a review can be activated at the request of an individual faculty member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional characteristics (size, mission), faculty preferences, and whether a blanket program is practical and constructive in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-benefit analysis and resource support
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure institutional resources can adequately support a meaningful and constructive system for post-tenure review without damage to academic programs or recognition of faculty merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-tenure review should be supported by resources for professional development and, if comprehensive review is used, tangible recognition for high or improved performance. Underfunded systems can become punitive or ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of faculty representatives and conformity with contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty representatives involved in development should be selected by the faculty and procedures should conform to any collective bargaining agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect existing governance arrangements and legal/contractual obligations when designing review bodies and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation records admissible but rebuttable
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation records may be used in later proceedings but are rebuttable as to accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even accurate records do not relieve the institution of the burden to prove adequate cause in a separate adversarial hearing; ensure mechanisms for correcting or contesting records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect time horizon for substantial scholarly work
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid shortening the time horizon of faculty by frequent reviews that incentivize safe, quick projects over more valuable long-term research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that serious professional undertakings require time; overly frequent/formal reviews can distort research choices and discourage high-risk, high-reward scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against grievance channels shifting burden to faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious when post-tenure review channels for challenging judgments place the burden of proving improper action on the faculty member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such grievance procedures can undermine academic freedom; ensure appeal mechanisms do not effectively reverse procedural protections by forcing faculty to prove institutional improper action.
